title: Review: The covalent model
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank, except where marked for IB Diploma Chemistry (status of the source: ai-reviewed-reverified-gate-verified-2026-09-30-awaiting-human-signoff). Terms and clues: S2.2#c25 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; S2.2#c30 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; S2.2#c17 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition; S2.2#c10 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition. Questions: S2.2#q35, S2.2#q05, S2.2#q08, S2.2#q09, S2.2#q11, S2.2#q16, S2.2#q19, S2.2#q21, S2.2#q07, S2.2#q40, S2.2#q10, S2.2#q13, S2.2#q23, S2.2#q25, S2.2#q27, S2.2#q29, S2.2#q31, S2.2#q33. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Intermolecular forces
items.clue: Attractive forces between molecules, as opposed to the covalent bonds within a molecule.

items.label: Van der Waals forces
items.clue: The inclusive term for dipole–dipole, dipole–induced dipole and London (dispersion) forces.

items.label: Covalent network structure
items.clue: A giant solid in which every atom is bonded to its neighbours throughout, with no separate molecules.

items.label: Electron domain
items.clue: A region of negative charge density around a central atom: a lone pair or any one link to a neighbour.

questions.stem: C₆₀ fullerene dissolves in methylbenzene, but diamond and graphite do not dissolve in any common solvent. Which statement explains the difference?

options.text: C₆₀ consists of separate molecules held by London forces; diamond and graphite are covalent networks
C₆₀ splits into ions in methylbenzene, but diamond and graphite cannot form ions
Diamond and graphite are held together by strong intermolecular forces between their atoms
Methylbenzene breaks the C–C bonds in C₆₀, which are weaker than those in diamond

questions.explanation: C₆₀ is a molecular allotrope: methylbenzene molecules can surround separate C₆₀ molecules, overcoming only the London forces between them. Diamond and graphite are covalent networks; dissolving them would mean breaking strong C–C covalent bonds.

questions.stem: Ammonia, NH₃, has three bonding pairs and one lone pair around the nitrogen atom. What is its molecular geometry?

options.text: Tetrahedral, as there are four electron domains around the nitrogen atom
Trigonal planar, as only the three bonding pairs repel one another
Flat, with 90° bond angles, as the atoms are drawn in its Lewis formula on paper
Trigonal pyramidal, as the lone pair occupies one of four tetrahedral domains

questions.explanation: The four electron domains take up a tetrahedral arrangement (electron-domain geometry). Only three are occupied by atoms, so the atoms form a pyramid with N at the apex: trigonal pyramidal, with H–N–H angles of about 107°.

questions.stem: Electronegativity values: H 2.2, C 2.6, O 3.4, F 4.0, P 2.2. Which bond is the most polar?

options.text: O–H
O–F
C–F
P–H

questions.explanation: The electronegativity difference is 4.0 − 2.6 = 1.4, the largest of the four, so the shared pair is drawn most unequally, towards F.

questions.stem: Carbon dioxide, CO₂, has no net dipole moment (electronegativity: C 2.6, O 3.4). Which statement explains this?

options.text: Its two C=O bond dipoles are equal and point in opposite directions, so they cancel
Its C=O bonds are non-polar, as the electronegativity difference is below 1.8
It carries no overall charge, so no separation of charge can exist in the molecule
Its carbon atom has no lone pair, and only lone pairs can produce a net dipole

questions.explanation: Each C=O bond is polar (difference 0.8, δ− on O). Carbon has two electron domains, so the molecule is linear and the two equal bond dipoles point in exactly opposite directions. Their vector sum is zero.

questions.stem: Graphite conducts electricity. Which feature of its structure explains this?

options.text: It contains carbon ions that move through the layers when a voltage is applied
Its atoms are held by metallic bonding, as its shiny grey appearance suggests
Each carbon atom bonds to three others, leaving one electron per atom delocalized
Its layers slide over one another easily, carrying electric charge as they move

questions.explanation: In each layer every carbon atom forms three covalent bonds. Its fourth valence electron is delocalized across the layer, and these mobile electrons carry the current along the layers.

questions.stem: Which statement about the intermolecular forces between molecules of propanone, CH₃COCH₃, is correct?

options.text: They include hydrogen bonds, as each propanone molecule contains H and O atoms
They include no London forces, as propanone molecules are polar
They include London forces, which are the only kind of van der Waals force
They include dipole–dipole forces, which count as van der Waals forces

questions.explanation: Propanone is polar: the C=O bond is polar and the bond dipoles do not cancel. So dipole–dipole forces act between its molecules, alongside London forces, and both are included in the term van der Waals forces.

questions.stem: Ethanol, CH₃CH₂OH, mixes with water in all proportions, but hexane, C₆H₁₄, does not dissolve in water. Which statement explains this difference?

options.text: Ethanol splits into ions that water surrounds, but hexane does not form ions
Ethanol can form hydrogen bonds with water molecules, but hexane cannot
Hexane is less dense than water, so it floats on the water rather than dissolving
Hexane molecules are too large to fit into the gaps between water molecules

questions.explanation: The O–H group of ethanol forms hydrogen bonds with water, replacing the hydrogen bonds broken between water molecules. Hexane forms only London forces with water, far weaker than the hydrogen bonds it would have to break, so it does not dissolve.

questions.stem: A mixture is separated by paper chromatography. Under the same conditions, component X has an RF value of 0.20 and component Y has an RF value of 0.75. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Relative to the mobile phase, X is attracted more strongly to the stationary phase than Y is
X has larger molecules than Y, so the fibres of the paper hold X back more than Y
X would also reach an RF of 0.75 if the solvent were allowed to run for a longer time
X is less soluble in the solvent than Y, and the paper plays no part in the separation

questions.stem: In methanal, H₂CO, the carbon atom forms a single bond to each of two hydrogen atoms and a double bond to the oxygen atom. What is the best prediction of the H–C–H bond angle?

options.text: About 109.5°, as the two bonds of C=O count as two separate electron domains
Slightly less than 120°, as the C=O double bond repels more than a single bond
Exactly 120°, as all three electron domains around carbon repel equally
About 104.5°, as oxygen's two lone pairs push the two C–H bonds together

questions.explanation: Carbon has three electron domains (two C–H bonds and the C=O bond), so the arrangement is trigonal planar. The double bond holds more electron density and repels the C–H bonds more strongly, so the H–C–H angle is squeezed slightly below 120° (to about 116°).

questions.stem: Electronegativity values: H 2.2, N 3.0. Which statement describes the N–H bond in ammonia, NH₃?

options.text: Each hydrogen atom has given its electron to nitrogen, so N³⁻ and H⁺ ions attract
The pair is shared equally, because a difference of 0.8 is too small to make a bond polar
Both atoms gain a share of the pair, so nitrogen and hydrogen are both δ−
The shared pair lies closer to nitrogen, so nitrogen is δ− and hydrogen is δ+

questions.explanation: Nitrogen (3.0) attracts the shared pair more strongly than hydrogen (2.2). Electron density shifts towards nitrogen, which carries a partial negative charge, δ−, leaving hydrogen with an equal partial positive charge, δ+.

questions.stem: Water, H₂O, has a net dipole moment (electronegativity: H 2.2, O 3.4). Which statement explains this?

options.text: Its O–H bonds are polar, and every molecule with polar bonds has a net dipole
It is bent, so its two O–H bond dipoles do not point in opposite directions
Its H atoms lie at 90° to each other, as in its Lewis formula, so the dipoles add
Its oxygen atom has two lone pairs, which are the only source of its net dipole

questions.explanation: Each O–H bond is polar (δ− on O). Oxygen's four electron domains (two of them lone pairs) make the molecule bent, about 104.5°, so the two bond dipoles add to give a resultant along the bisector of the angle.

questions.stem: Carbon dioxide sublimes at −78 °C, but silicon dioxide melts at about 1700 °C. Which statement explains the difference?

options.text: Subliming CO₂ breaks its C=O bonds, which are weaker than the Si–O bonds in SiO₂
SiO₂ molecules are heavier than CO₂ molecules, so their London forces are stronger
SiO₂ is a giant covalent network, but CO₂ is made of small separate molecules
SiO₂ is an ionic solid of Si⁴⁺ and O²⁻ ions, like other oxides with high melting points

questions.explanation: In SiO₂ each Si atom is covalently bonded to four O atoms and each O atom to two Si atoms, so melting breaks many strong covalent bonds. CO₂ is made of separate molecules, and subliming it overcomes only weak London forces between them.

questions.stem: In the ethanoate ion, CH₃COO⁻, the carbon atom of the COO group is bonded to the CH₃ carbon and to both O atoms. How many resonance structures can be deduced for the ethanoate ion?

options.text: 0 structures, as the atoms bonded to the central C are not all the same
3 structures, as C can also form double bonds to both O atoms at once
2 structures, as the C=O double bond can be drawn to either O atom
4 structures, as an H atom can also move from CH₃ onto either O atom

questions.explanation: The COO carbon is bonded to CH₃ and to two equivalent O atoms. The C=O double bond can be drawn to either O, with the −1 charge on the other, giving two resonance structures that differ only in the position of the double bond; the real ion is their hybrid, with two identical C–O bonds.

questions.stem: Cyclohexene reacts with bromine by addition. Benzene reacts with bromine only in the presence of a catalyst, and then by substitution, forming C₆H₅Br and HBr. Which statement explains why benzene undergoes substitution rather than addition?

options.text: Benzene has no π electrons at all, so like an alkane it can only take part in substitution
Substitution leaves benzene's delocalized ring of π electrons, and its stability, intact
Benzene contains three C=C bonds that are far stronger than the C=C bond in cyclohexene itself
Benzene's C=C bonds move around the ring too quickly for bromine to add across them

questions.stem: In xenon tetrafluoride, XeF₄, the xenon atom (eight valence electrons) forms a single bond to each of four fluorine atoms. What is the molecular geometry of XeF₄?

options.text: Tetrahedral, as only its four bonding pairs repel one another around the Xe atom
Octahedral, as there are six electron domains around the xenon atom
Square planar, as the two lone pairs occupy opposite positions of an octahedron
See-saw, as the two lone pairs occupy adjacent positions, 90° apart, in an octahedron

questions.explanation: Xenon uses four electrons in bonds and keeps two lone pairs: six electron domains, octahedral. The two lone pairs repel most strongly, so they sit opposite each other, leaving the four F atoms in a square plane.

questions.stem: Two Lewis formulas are proposed for CO₂. In formula I, each O atom is joined to C by a double bond and has two lone pairs. In formula II, one O atom is joined to C by a triple bond and has one lone pair, and the other O atom is joined by a single bond and has three lone pairs. Which formula is preferred, and why?

options.text: Formula I, as the sum of all its formal charges is zero
Formula II, as it places a negative formal charge on an oxygen atom
Formula II, as its triple bond is stronger than any double bond
Formula I, as every atom in it has a formal charge of zero

questions.explanation: Formula I: C 4 − 0 − 4 = 0; each O 6 − 4 − 2 = 0. Formula II: triple-bonded O 6 − 2 − 3 = +1, C 0, single-bonded O 6 − 6 − 1 = −1. Formula I has formal charges closest to zero, so it is preferred.

questions.stem: Carbon dioxide has the Lewis formula O=C=O. How many σ and π bonds does one CO₂ molecule contain?

options.text: Four σ bonds and zero π bonds
Two σ bonds and two π bonds
No σ bond and four π bonds
Two σ bonds and no π bond

questions.explanation: Each C=O double bond is one σ bond (head-on overlap along the axis) and one π bond (lateral overlap of p orbitals). Two double bonds give 2 σ and 2 π.

questions.stem: Which statement about hybridization in an inorganic species is correct?

options.text: The nitrogen atom in NH₃ is not hybridized, as only carbon forms hybrid orbitals
The carbon atom in CO₂ is sp³ hybridized, as it forms 4 bonds in total
The carbon atom in HCN forms its two π bonds from sp hybrid orbitals
The boron atom in BF₃ is sp² hybridized, with its three hybrid orbitals at 120°

questions.explanation: Boron has three electron domains (three B–F bonds, no lone pair), so it is sp² hybridized and the three hybrid orbitals lie in a plane at 120°, giving the trigonal planar shape.
